page: Amazon Web Services c5n.9xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 36 dedicated vCPUs derived from 18 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at a base frequency of 3.4 GHz. Hardware acceleration capabilities include AVX and AVX-512 vector extensions, AES cryptography, and bit manipulation instructions like BMI2, ADX, and FMA. Memory is provisioned at 96.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, which equates to roughly 2.67 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle any local instance storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage solutions such as Amazon EBS. Its standout networking configuration provides a baseline throughput of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the c5n.9xlarge squarely within mid-tier performance across general compute and memory evaluations. The instance recorded a multi-core score of 33,340.81 in stress-ng and 10,778.0 in Geekbench, backed by a PassMark CPU score of 30,123.3. Memory throughput tests reveal an uncached read rate of 104.3 GB/sec and a write rate of 45.03 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads achieve 1,853.99 GB/sec. Data processing tests show solid operational capacity, sustaining 32.41 million Redis SET operations per second and 21.71 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Machine learning inference on small 135M parameter models demonstrates 1,846.91 prompt tokens per second, but drops noticeably to 5.27 tokens per second on large 70B parameter models, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5n.9xlarge provides high network bandwidth density alongside compute capacity without requiring users to pay for unused local NVMe storage or specialized accelerator hardware. However, because local storage is absent, overall operational efficiency depends on EBS provisioning and throughput alignment. The instance is suited for compute-intensive workloads that require substantial network throughput, including network traffic inspection, distributed data analytics, clustered CI/CD compilation, and medium-scale web serving.
